questions.question:
Transform the affirmative sentence into a negative sentence without changing its meaning:
"The senior magistrate is a very impartial officer."

options.text: The senior magistrate is not an impartial officer.
The senior magistrate is not a partial officer.
The senior magistrate is never a fair officer.
Is the senior magistrate not a partial officer?

questions.explanation: Affirmative sentence mein 'impartial' (nispaksh) quality describe ki gayi hai. Negative transformation mein helping verb 'is' ke baad 'not' lagaya aur 'impartial' ko uske antonym 'partial' (pakshpaati) se replace kiya ('is not a partial officer'). Isse original meaning 100% same rehta hai. Option (A) mein antonym use nahi kiya gaya jisse meaning ulta ho gaya. Option (C) mein 'never a fair officer' galat negation hai. Option (D) interrogative form hai, negative assertive nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Antonym Negation (Not + Opposite Word).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Choose the correct negative transformation of the sentence:
"Only authorized advocates can enter the judges' library."

options.text: None but authorized advocates can enter the judges' library.
Nothing but authorized advocates can enter the judges' library.
Not more than authorized advocates can enter the judges' library.
Authorized advocates cannot enter the judges' library.

questions.explanation: Sentence mein 'Only' persons ('authorized advocates') par lag raha hai. Rule ke anusaar, jab 'only' persons ke liye use hota hai toh negative transformation 'None but' se start hota hai: 'None but authorized advocates can enter...'. Option (B) mein 'Nothing but' inanimate objects ke liye use hota hai, persons ke liye nahi. Option (C) mein 'Not more than' age ya numbers ke liye use hota hai. Option (D) direct negation hai jo permission ko deny kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Only / Alone Substitution (None but for persons).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform into a negative sentence without altering the original meaning:
"The petitioner demanded only justice from the High Court."

options.text: The petitioner demanded none but justice from the High Court.
The petitioner demanded nothing but justice from the High Court.
The petitioner did not demand any justice from the High Court.
The petitioner demanded not only justice from the High Court.

questions.explanation: 'Justice' ek abstract noun / non-person entity hai. Jab 'only' kisi inanimate concept ya thing par apply ho, toh uski negative transformation 'nothing but' se hoti hai: 'The petitioner demanded nothing but justice...'. Option (A) mein 'none but' persons ke liye reserved hai. Option (C) meaning ko deny kar deta hai ('did not demand any justice'). Option (D) incomplete correlative structure banata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Only / Alone Substitution (Nothing but for things).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform the sentence into a negative structure:
"As soon as the registrar called the roll, the candidates answered."

options.text: No sooner did the registrar call the roll when the candidates answered.
No sooner did the registrar call the roll than the candidates answered.
No sooner had the registrar called the roll then the candidates answered.
No sooner the registrar called the roll than the candidates answered.

questions.explanation: 'As soon as' clause ko negative transformation mein 'No sooner' se invert kiya jata hai. Structure: 'No sooner did + Subject + V1 + than ...'. Auxiliary 'did' aane par verb 'call' (V1) aayegi, aur connecting conjunction STRICTLY 'than' aayega. Option (A) mein fatal error 'when' lagaya gaya hai. Option (C) mein 'then' lagaya gaya hai jo incorrect hai. Option (D) mein auxiliary inversion miss kar diya gaya ('No sooner the registrar...'). Option (B) 100% correct hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Temporal Inversion (No sooner did...than).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.subtopic: Universal Affirmatives ('Every' ➔ 'There is no...who does not')
questions.question:
Which of the following is the correct negative transformation of:
"Every law student respects the Constitution of India."

options.text: There is no law student who respects the Constitution of India.
There is no law student who does not respect the Constitution of India.
No law student does not respect the Constitution of India.
Not every law student respects the Constitution of India.

questions.explanation: Universal affirmative statement 'Every law student respects...' ko negative clause 'There is no law student' aur negative relative clause 'who does not respect...' se transform kiya jata hai. Dono negatives milkar affirmative proposition ('every student respects') ko exactly match karte hain. Option (A) meaning ko ulta kar deta hai (ki koi student respect nahi karta). Option (C) unnatural phrasing hai. Option (D) claim ko partial bana deta hai ('Not every' = some don't), jo original universal claim ko weaken karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Universal Affirmative (There is no...who does not).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform the sentence by removing 'too':
"The clerk was too exhausted to verify the remaining case registers."

options.text: The clerk was so exhausted that he cannot verify the remaining case registers.
The clerk was so exhausted that he could not verify the remaining case registers.
The clerk was so exhausted to verify the remaining case registers.
The clerk was very exhausted that he could not verify the remaining case registers.

questions.explanation: 'Too + adjective + to + V1' ko 'so + adjective + that + Subject + modal + V1' mein transform kiya jata hai. Kyunki main verb 'was' Past tense mein hai, isliye that-clause mein Past ability modal 'could not' aayega ('could not verify'). Option (A) mein 'cannot' present tense hai jo past governing verb 'was' ke sath tense discord create karta hai. Option (C) incomplete correlation hai. Option (D) mein 'very...that' non-standard syntax hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Intensive Inability (Too...to ➔ So...that could not).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform the assertive statement into an interrogative sentence:
"Knowledge is immense power in administrative law."

options.text: Is knowledge immense power in administrative law?
Is knowledge not immense power in administrative law?
Was knowledge not immense power in administrative law?
Knowledge is not immense power in administrative law?

questions.explanation: Golden Polarity Law ke anusaar, affirmative assertive statement interrogative bante waqt negative question banta hai. Helping verb 'is' ko subject 'knowledge' se pehle invert kiya aur negative particle 'not' lagaya ('Is knowledge not immense power...?'). Option (A) positive question hai jo inquiry/doubt show karta hai, assertion affirm nahi karta. Option (C) mein tense past 'was' kar diya gaya jo invalid hai. Option (D) declarative word order retain karta hai bina auxiliary inversion ke.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: The Golden Polarity Law (Affirmative Statement ➔ Negative Question).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform the sentence into an interrogative form:
"The High Court ordered a fresh judicial inquiry into the matter."

options.text: Did the High Court order a fresh judicial inquiry into the matter?
Did the High Court not order a fresh judicial inquiry into the matter?
Did the High Court not ordered a fresh judicial inquiry into the matter?
Has the High Court not ordered a fresh judicial inquiry into the matter?

questions.explanation: Original sentence Simple Past tense ('ordered' V2) mein affirmative assertive hai. Polarity flip ke liye negative interrogative banana hoga: dummy auxiliary 'Did' subject 'The High Court' se pehle aayegi, 'not' lagega, aur main verb base form V1 'order' mein restore hogi ('Did the High Court not order...?'). Option (A) positive question hai. Option (C) mein 'did' ke baad V2 'ordered' chhod diya gaya jo double past error hai. Option (D) tense badal kar Present Perfect 'has' kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Dummy Auxiliary Inversion (Did + S + not + V1?).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Convert the negative statement into an interrogative sentence:
"No one can question the integrity of the Chief Justice."

options.text: Can anyone question the integrity of the Chief Justice?
Cannot anyone question the integrity of the Chief Justice?
Can no one question the integrity of the Chief Justice?
Who cannot question the integrity of the Chief Justice?

questions.explanation: Original statement negative hai ('No one can question...'). Polarity Law ke anusaar, negative statement interrogative bante waqt affirmative question banta hai. Negative pronoun 'No one' affirmative pronoun 'anyone' mein badal jata hai aur modal 'can' invert hota hai: 'Can anyone question...?'. Is question ka implied answer hai 'No, no one can'. Option (B) mein 'cannot' lagane se meaning ulta ho jata hai. Option (C) redundant negative retain karta hai. Option (D) 'Who cannot' implies karta hai ki sab question kar sakte hain, jo bilkul ulta meaning hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Rhetorical Quantifier Equivalence (No one ➔ Can anyone?).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Choose the semantically equivalent interrogative form of:
"Everyone desires peace and judicial transparency in society."

options.text: Who desires peace and judicial transparency in society?
Who does not desire peace and judicial transparency in society?
Does everyone desire peace and judicial transparency in society?
Why does everyone desire peace and judicial transparency in society?

questions.explanation: 'Everyone desires...' universal affirmative claim hai. Iska rhetorical equivalent negative question 'Who does not desire...?' hota hai (Kyunki is question ka obvious rhetorical answer nikalta hai: 'Everyone does'). Option (A) 'Who desires...?' implies karta hai 'Nobody desires', jo original truth value ka exact opposite hai. Option (C) normal information query ban jati hai jo statement ki surety ko khatam kar deti hai. Option (D) reason poochne wala Wh-question ban jata hai jo transformation scope se bahar hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Rhetorical Quantifier Equivalence (Everyone ➔ Who does not).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Transform the exclamatory sentence into an assertive sentence:
"How prompt the court assistant was in issuing the certified copy!"

options.text: The court assistant was very prompt in issuing the certified copy.
The court assistant was prompt in issuing the certified copy!
Was the court assistant very prompt in issuing the certified copy?
The court assistant was a great prompt in issuing the certified copy.

questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentence 'How prompt...' mein 'prompt' ek adjective hai. Adjective ko intensify karne ke liye assertive sentence mein adverb 'very' lagaya jata hai, subject 'The court assistant' aur verb 'was' sentence ke shuru mein aate hain, aur exclamation mark (!) full stop (.) mein badalta hai: 'The court assistant was very prompt...'. Option (B) mein intensity marker 'very' missing hai aur exclamation mark chhod diya gaya hai. Option (C) interrogative form hai. Option (D) mein adjective ke sath 'a great' galat collocation hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Exclamatory Intensifier Matching ('How' + Adj ➔ 'Very').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08

questions.question:
Convert into an assertive statement:
"What a tragedy the destruction of historical court archives was!"

options.text: The destruction of historical court archives was a very tragedy.
The destruction of historical court archives was a terrible tragedy.
The destruction of historical court archives was tragedy.
Was the destruction of historical court archives a terrible tragedy?

questions.explanation: 'Tragedy' ek noun of magnitude hai. Noun ko intensify karne ke liye adverb 'very' use nahi hota ('*a very tragedy' is grammatically incorrect). Noun ke aage contextually suitable adjective jaise 'terrible', 'great', ya 'dreadful' use kiya jata hai: 'The destruction of historical court archives was a terrible tragedy.' Option (A) mein fatal intensifier blunder 'a very tragedy' hai. Option (C) mein intensifier drop kar diya gaya jisse sentence ka emphasis khatam ho gaya. Option (D) interrogative structure hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Exclamatory Intensifier Matching (Noun ➔ 'Terrible / Great').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L08
